images.caption: Figure 1:Serving food to a vegetarian user. (1) The user asks only, “Serve me food.” (2) CarryOn retrieves the context from memory. (3) The planner dispatches a sequence of subtasks to a frozen VLA policy: open the pink cover and, if the carrot is underneath, place it in the bowl. (4) During execution, a proactive shield steers the gripper and the carried carrot around an obstacle, and reactive recovery re-grasps the carrot to resume the task.

Figure 3:(a) Schematic of the perturbation, varying object displacement relative to the initial lifted position.
(b) Policy-only response to object displacement on LIBERO-Object. Blue bars show task success, and the upper line shows the decrease from undisturbed success in percentage points.

Figure 4:Simulation settings.(a)–(d) RoboLab scenes for personalized planning and memory revision; (e)–(f) LIBERO-Safety tasks for proactive shielding; (g)–(h) controlled perturbations in LIBERO and recorded failure states in LIBERO-Recovery.

Figure 5:Real-robot settings.A Franka Research 3 with external and wrist-mounted cameras. (a) Covered-ingredient retrieval before and after lid opening; (b) sandwich preparation; (c) activity-dependent packing; (d) safe execution; (e) failure recovery.

Figure 6:Integrated food-serving runs.(a)–(d) Memory-guided lid opening and shielded transport. (e)–(h) Recovery restores a lost grasp before task completion. (i)–(l) Revealing meat triggers a scene-memory update and refusal under the vegetarian preference.

images.caption: Figure 7:Geometric action filtering and retreat.Each example shows a geometric side view (left), the observed scene (upper right), and predicted gripper–obstacle distances (lower right); gray spheres depict current robot geometry and purple outlines depict predicted gripper geometry. (a) Actions before the first violation of the dashed distance threshold are released; (b) if the first action is blocked, the robot retreats and rechecks. Open triangles mark obstacle points nearest the predicted gripper surface for filtering, whereas the filled trianglennis nearest the current end-effector reference point and determines retreat. The two thin dashed arrows in (b), arranged head-to-tail, show the component away fromnnand the added upward bias; the thick solid arrow shows their resulting retreat direction.
